sections.h2: Which Jefferson County offices deal with property tax?
sections.html:
Jefferson County splits the job among town and city assessors, local tax collectors and two county offices in Watertown. Local assessors set values, towns, villages and school districts bill, and the county steps in when a bill turns delinquent. The City of Watertown is excluded from the county's collection and tax mapping work.

Real Property Tax Services is open 8 am to 5 pm, and 8 am to 4 pm in July and August.

sections.h2: How to pay a Jefferson County tax bill
sections.html:
Start with a call to the Treasurer at 315-785-3055 or an email to treasurer@jeffersoncountyny.gov. Verify the amount and the collector before you pay, because the office rejects and returns a payment sent for the wrong amount or to the wrong collector.

  • By mail or in person at 175 Arsenal Street, Watertown, NY 13601, with checks payable to the Jefferson County Treasurer.
  • Online, using the tax map number or 911 address plus the installment number as the ID. Cards carry a 3.0% fee plus 69 cents, and American Express is not taken.
  • Village and school bills go to the village or the school district named on the bill.

Treasurer hours are 9 am to 5 pm from September 1 through June 30, with collections until 4:45 pm. In July and August the hours are 8:30 am to 4 pm. The date full town and county payments open changes from year to year, so ask when the current year's collection begins.

sections.h2: Challenging an assessment in Jefferson County
sections.html:
File Form RP-524 with the assessor or Board of Assessment Review in your town or city by Grievance Day. In most New York communities that day is the fourth Tuesday in May, which is May 25 in 2027, but confirm it with your local assessor or municipal clerk.

Filing is free and needs no lawyer. Only the assessment on the current tentative roll can be grieved. If the board turns you down, an owner-occupied home qualifies for Small Claims Assessment Review at $30, started within 30 days after the final roll is filed. Villages that assess their own property keep separate dates, usually in February, so a village homeowner may have two assessments to check.

The county office can help local assessors on valuations, small claims hearings and rolls, while the local board hears the grievance itself. Call Real Property Tax Services at 315-785-3074 with questions about a parcel's tax map or address.

sections.h2: What happens when Jefferson County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
The county can foreclose, and its FAQ describes how to stop it. A parcel is saved by paying every delinquent tax, interest, penalty and fee before the redemption date, or by signing an installment agreement for owners who qualify.

  • An installment agreement requires 25% down on all delinquent amounts for the owner's county properties outside Watertown, then eight roughly equal quarterly payments over two years, with new taxes paid in full and on time.
  • An owner is eligible once at least 30 days late, but not after defaulting on an earlier agreement or losing property to foreclosure within three years.
  • State law requires redeeming the newest taxes first, so paying only the oldest year does not remove a parcel from the list.
  • Deadlines are firm, and extensions are not possible. Only a majority vote of the County Legislature can waive penalties and interest.

Once the county takes title at foreclosure, the former owner's interest ends. The county generally offers the property at its annual tax auction, selling as-is by quitclaim deed, and an auction buyer takes on the school and village tax for the auction year. Buyers may face unpaid water, sewer or utility bills, easements and zoning limits, and the county gives no guarantee about boundaries or size. For a seller, that is a reason to resolve the tax before the parcel reaches the auction list.

sections.h2: What to do about Jefferson County tax before selling
sections.html:
Tax liens follow the property, so a buyer inherits the bill even if the seller never mentions it. A seller with delinquent tax should get a written payoff from the Treasurer and settle it from the sale proceeds, or sell before the foreclosure date.

  1. Ask the town, village or school collector for the current-year status.
  2. Ask the Treasurer for the delinquent balance with interest through the closing date.
  3. Tell the title company about any installment agreement so the remaining balance is paid off at closing.

A third party who pays your tax does not gain the house, since the old tax sale certificate practice ended years ago. An owner who inherited a home in Le Ray, Clayton or Adams and fell behind does not have to wait for an auction. A cash sale can bring the tax current in one closing. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff letter that runs through your expected closing date, since interest keeps accruing until the day the money arrives.

sections.h2: Jefferson County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Jefferson County sits on New York's northern border where the St. Lawrence River leaves Lake Ontario. Watertown is the county seat, and Le Ray is the largest town, with a 2020 count of 25,574. The Fort Drum base brings a steady stream of buyers and renters. Villages include Carthage, West Carthage, Clayton, Adams, Sackets Harbor, Alexandria Bay and Cape Vincent.

The county has an estimated 111,540 residents as of July 2025, down 4.4% from the 2020 base, across 62,392 housing units. Homeowners occupy 54.7% of units, the median owner-occupied value is $188,200, and median rent is $1,213. Median household income is $66,301. Summer tourism lifts the population noticeably, so a listing that sits through the winter can look different in July.

faqs.q: Who collects delinquent property tax in Jefferson County, NY?
faqs.a: The County Treasurer collects delinquent village, school, town and county real property tax, except in the City of Watertown. The office is at 175 Arsenal Street in Watertown, 315-785-3055.

faqs.q: Can I get an extension on Jefferson County foreclosure deadlines?
faqs.a: No. All deadlines are firm. The only ways to save the property are paying everything owed before the redemption date or entering an installment agreement.

faqs.q: How does a Jefferson County installment agreement work?
faqs.a: You pay 25% of all delinquent taxes, interest, fees and penalties up front, then eight roughly equal quarterly payments over two years. You must also keep all new taxes current.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in Jefferson County?
faqs.a: In most New York communities it is the fourth Tuesday in May, which is May 25 in 2027. Confirm the date with your town or city assessor, since villages and some cities differ.

faqs.q: Does paying someone else's delinquent tax give me their Jefferson County property?
faqs.a: No. The sale of tax certificates ended years ago, and ownership stays with the owner of record no matter who pays.
